actionable.title: Reject non-regular entries in policy globs instead of silently omitting them
actionable.problem: policy_inventory skips every non-regular glob match without recording an error. Adding a POSIX FIFO .pi/agents/unreviewed.md alongside an approved regular agent leaves the observed policy map identical to the pinned manifest. scan_workspace also accepts this object. The real CLI then invokes tool probes and emits required_ok=true despite an additional unreviewed policy input capable of supplying bytes through a FIFO. This defeats the exact policy-path-set gate for filesystem object types the scanner currently accepts.
actionable.fix: Fail the policy inventory on unsupported non-regular matches (at least FIFOs, sockets and device nodes), preserving any explicitly intended directory exclusions such as bootstrap __pycache__. Add a regression with an unchanged approved pin and an added FIFO asserting failed scope/baseline and no tool probes.
actionable.reproduction: adversarial/reproduce.py uses an exact-byte copy of the reviewed verifier, a real synthetic Git repository, a fixed synthetic approved manifest and harmless shell executables for node/pi/uv; no verifier function is mocked. Control exits 0; after os.mkfifo(root / ".pi/agents/unreviewed.md"), the CLI again exits 0. adversarial/results.json records required_ok=true, baseline_match_not_runtime_approval, inventory_errors=0, unexpected_paths=[], scan_errors=0 and actual probe calls.

actionable.title: Reject special files before opening the approval manifest
actionable.problem: policy_baseline_check rejects a symlink but opens other filesystem objects with a blocking read. Supplying a FIFO as --policy-manifest hangs indefinitely waiting for a writer before the size limit or digest validation runs. The workspace scan time budget is already over and cannot stop this call; no failure receipt is produced. This allows a malformed or replaced approval-manifest path to stall the verifier rather than fail closed.
actionable.fix: Validate the manifest is a regular file before reading, and use an open/fstat strategy that cannot block on a substituted FIFO (for example a nonblocking, no-follow open where available followed by a regular-file check). Add a POSIX FIFO regression that completes promptly with invalid_or_unreadable_manifest and writes the failure receipt.
actionable.reproduction: The final case in adversarial/reproduce.py invokes the actual copied CLI with a FIFO manifest and a syntactically valid digest. subprocess.run(timeout=2) raises TimeoutExpired and terminates the harmless verifier process; adversarial/results.json records timeoutSeconds=2 and receiptExists=false. No network, credentials, installs or repository writes are involved.
